audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance was written as a generic 'W shield/heal' that 'blocks your burst'. It specifically reduces PHYSICAL damage while she charges — and Kled's entire kit is physical, so it blunts all of it rather than part of it. The full layer also wrote 'Beartrap', used 'his'/'him' for Irelia, and never named an ability outside Flawless Duet.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'Irelia charges a strike that deals more damage as she charges. She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Riot's Q text: Bladesurge heals her and refreshes its cooldown on a Marked target or a kill, which is why she resets through a big wave. Riot's E text: two blades converge, damaging, stunning and Marking — nothing about the E healing or shielding.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance named with its 20s rank-1 cooldown and its physical-damage cut stated explicitly in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], phases[3].why and wants.foe[2]; Bladesurge named as the reset in the don'ts and itemization.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six chart rows were inverted against the packet and against the page's own prose — rows 2 through 5 all read Kled or Skill while whys[2] to whys[5] each describe Irelia controlling the trade, and Level 1 read Skill while whys[0] was actually written about level 2.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Kled / Skill / Irelia / Irelia / Irelia / Irelia / Kled, and the mirror audit states rows 0-5 were flipped to exactly that in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 flipped in matched full/content pairs, ratings moved with them, the four contradicting phases whys rewritten, and whys[0] rewritten so the level-1 row is actually about level 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet was tracked with no cooldown number, and the reason it beats you was never stated.
audit.why: It is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and a stun. Kled's E dashes out and recasts back; a stun between the two halves strands you inside her reset range, and it also cancels the Violent Tendencies shot sequence.
audit.corrected: The 16s number and the re-E cancel written into the cooldown block, dosFull[0], report[5] and phases[1].why.

notes: Irelia's E carries a 'grounding' derived flag in the kit file, but Riot's Flawless Duet text describes only damage, a stun and a Mark — no grounding. Per the description-over-flag rule I made no grounding claim; the stun alone is enough to cancel the re-E. The single most useful fact this page was missing is that Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage specifically: Kled has no magic damage anywhere, so an up W blunts one hundred percent of his combo, which is the real reason levels 3-6 belong to her.
